content.text: {"predictors": [{"name": "Supplier Concentration Fragility", "construction": "From the 10-K, count the number of major suppliers or customers disclosed under SFAS 131 segment/customer disclosures. Compute a Herfindahl index of revenue dependence on the largest disclosed customers (percent of sales to customers exceeding 10% threshold). Rank firms cross-sectionally by this concentration each June using prior fiscal-year filings.", "rationale": "Firms dependent on few large customers bear concentrated demand and bargaining-power risk that is underpriced by investors focused on aggregate revenue growth.", "higher_returns_for": "high customer concentration (as compensation for undiversified demand risk)"}, {"name": "Accrual Volatility", "construction": "For each firm compute total accruals (change in non-cash current assets minus change in current liabilities excluding short-term debt, minus depreciation) scaled by average total assets for each of the prior 5 fiscal years. Take the standard deviation of this series. Rank firms cross-sectionally in June.", "rationale": "Unstable accruals signal low earnings quality and estimation uncertainty; investors underappreciate the persistence advantage of firms with smooth accrual generation.", "higher_returns_for": "low accrual volatility"}, {"name": "Order Backlog Growth", "construction": "Extract reported order backlog (Compustat item ORDB or from 10-K where available) and compute year-over-year growth in backlog scaled by lagged total assets. Form deciles each June.", "rationale": "Backlog is a forward-looking demand indicator that is slowly incorporated into prices because it is not a headline income-statement figure.", "higher_returns_for": "high backlog growth"}, {"name": "R&D Acceleration", "construction": "Compute the change in R&D-to-sales ratio between the two most recent fiscal years minus the change over the prior two years (second difference of R&D intensity). Rank firms with positive R&D cross-sectionally each June.", "rationale": "Accelerating innovation investment predicts future intangible payoffs that markets discount too heavily given conservative accounting expensing of R&D.", "higher_returns_for": "high (positive) R&D acceleration"}, {"name": "Working Capital Efficiency Trend", "construction": "Compute the cash conversion cycle (days inventory + days receivables - days payables) for the current and prior fiscal year. Measure the year-over-year improvement (decrease). Rank firms cross-sectionally each June by improvement.", "rationale": "Managers who tighten working capital signal operational discipline and free up cash flow that the market recognizes only gradually.", "higher_returns_for": "large improvement (decrease) in cash conversion cycle"}, {"name": "Dispersion of Intraday Return Signs", "construction": "Using daily CRSP data over the prior 12 months, compute the fraction of positive-return days minus negative-return days, then measure how clustered runs are versus random using a runs-test z-statistic. Rank firms by the runs-test statistic each month.", "rationale": "Non-random clustering of return signs reflects sluggish information diffusion among a limited investor base, predicting continued drift.", "higher_returns_for": "high positive-run clustering"}, {"name": "Seasonality-Adjusted Volume Shock", "construction": "For each month compute average daily dollar volume, deseasonalize by subtracting the same calendar-month average over the prior 3 years, and scale by its historical standard deviation. Rank firms each month by this volume z-score.", "rationale": "Abnormal volume relative to a stock's own seasonal norm reveals arriving information not yet reflected in price, generating short-horizon continuation.", "higher_returns_for": "high positive volume shock"}, {"name": "Deferred Revenue Buildup", "construction": "Compute year-over-year change in deferred/unearned revenue (Compustat) scaled by lagged sales. Rank firms cross-sectionally each June.", "rationale": "Growth in deferred revenue represents prepaid future sales already collected in cash, an underappreciated leading indicator of recognized revenue and cash-flow quality.", "higher_returns_for": "high deferred revenue growth"}, {"name": "Capital Expenditure Smoothness", "construction": "Compute capex-to-assets for each of the prior 5 years and take the coefficient of variation. Rank firms cross-sectionally each June by inverse volatility.", "rationale": "Firms with steady, disciplined investment programs avoid value-destroying overinvestment cycles; markets overweight lumpy expansion stories.", "higher_returns_for": "low capex volatility (smooth investment)"}, {"name": "Gross Margin Stability Premium", "construction": "Compute gross margin (sales minus COGS over sales) for the prior 8 quarters and take the standard deviation. Combine into a signal that ranks firms by low margin volatility conditional on above-median margin level, each June.", "rationale": "Persistent, stable gross margins indicate durable competitive moats and pricing power that the market undervalues relative to reported growth.", "higher_returns_for": "low gross margin volatility with high margin level"}]}
